claim: The absence of 'shovel-ready' anti-coronavirus drugs during vaccine development has exceedingly worsened the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic.
source: The absence of 'shovel-ready' anti-coronavirus drugs during vaccine development has exceedingly worsened the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic.
evidence: This is a statement made in the abstract about the impact of lack of antiviral drugs on the pandemic.

claim: RDV incorporation does not terminate viral RNA synthesis, but leads the polymerase into backtrack as far as 30 nt.
source: We show that RDV incorporation does not terminate viral RNA synthesis, but leads the polymerase into backtrack as far as 30 nt, which may appear as termination in traditional ensemble assays.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from magnetic tweezers assays showing polymerase backtracking upon RDV incorporation.

claim: SARS-CoV-2 is able to evade the endogenously synthesized product of the viperin antiviral protein, ddhCTP.
source: SARS-CoV-2 is able to evade the endogenously synthesized product of the viperin antiviral protein, ddhCTP, though the polymerase incorporates this NA well.
evidence: This claim is supported by cell-based assays showing no antiviral effect of ddhC despite good incorporation in vitro.

claim: The coronavirus polymerase is composed of the nsp12 RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp), and the nsp7 and nsp8 co-factors, with a stoichiometry of 1:1:2.
source: The coronavirus polymerase is composed of the nsp12 RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp), and the nsp7 and nsp8 co-factors, with a stoichiometry of 1:1:2 (Kirchdoerfer and Ward, 2019; Hillen et al., 2020; Gao et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous structural and biochemical studies.

claim: The nsp14 proofreads the terminus of the nascent RNA following synthesis by the polymerase and associated factors.
source: The latter proofreads the terminus of the nascent RNA following synthesis by the polymerase and associated factors (Robson et al., 2020), a unique feature of coronaviruses relative to all other families of RNA viruses.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work on coronavirus proofreading.

claim: Proofreading likely contributes to the stability of the unusually large, ~30 kb, coronavirus genome.
source: Proofreading likely contributes to the stability of the unusually large, ~30 kb, coronavirus genome.
evidence: This is an inference based on the known function of proofreading and the large genome size.

claim: Remdesivir (RDV) is a recently discovered NA that showed efficacy against Ebola infection.
source: Remdesivir (RDV) is a recently discovered NA that showed efficacy against Ebola infection (Siegel et al., 2017) and has been successfully repurposed for the treatment of SARS-CoV-2 infection (Agostini et al., 2018; Gordon et al., 2020a; Gordon et al., 2020b; Pruijssers and Denison, 2019; Jockusch et al., 2020; Chien et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies on remdesivir efficacy.

claim: The success of RDV relies on its efficient incorporation by the polymerase and probable evasion of the proofreading machinery.
source: The success of RDV relies on its efficient incorporation by the polymerase (Gordon et al., 2020b; Dangerfield et al., 2020) and probable evasion of the proofreading machinery (Agostini et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies on RDV mechanism of action.

claim: Increasing the temperature from 25°C to 37°C results in a twofold decrease in the median replication time for SARS-CoV-2 polymerase.
source: Increasing the temperature from 25°C to 37°C, SARS-CoV-2 polymerase reveals a strong temperature dependence, which translates into a twofold decrease in the median replication time (Figure 1E), while not affecting the RNA synthesis product length (Figure 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Temperature increase from 25°C to 37°C does not affect the RNA synthesis product length of SARS-CoV-2 polymerase.
source: Increasing the temperature from 25°C to 37°C, SARS-CoV-2 polymerase reveals a strong temperature dependence, which translates into a twofold decrease in the median replication time (Figure 1E), while not affecting the RNA synthesis product length (Figure 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: 3'-dATP is an obligatory terminator of RNA chain elongation for viral RdRp.
source: 3′-dATP is an obligatory terminator of RNA chain elongation for viral RdRp (Gohara et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work on 3'-dATP.

claim: In the presence of 500 µM NTP and 500 µM 3′-dATP, the ability of the SARS-CoV-2 polymerase to reach the end of the template (1043 nt) was compromised.
source: In the presence of 500 µM NTP and 500 µM 3′-dATP, the ability of the SARS-CoV-2 polymerase to reach the end of the template (1043 nt) was compromised (Figure 2A vs. Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A compared to Figure 1B.

claim: 3′-dATP utilizes the NAB pathway for incorporation.
source: Therefore, we conclude that 3′-dATP utilizes the NAB pathway for incorporation (Figure 1D).
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the stoichiometry-dependent incorporation pattern.

claim: RDV-TP is an adenine analog with a 1′-cyano modification that has been shown to outcompete ATP for incorporation.
source: RDV-TP is an adenine analog with a 1′-cyano modification that has recently been shown to outcompete ATP for incorporation (Gordon et al., 2020b; Dangerfield et al., 2020; Figure 2—figure supplement 1), while exhibiting a low cytotoxicity (Pruijssers et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies and chemical structure shown in supplementary figure.

claim: RDV-TP has been proposed to induce delayed chain termination at i+3 during RNA synthesis by the core polymerase.
source: RDV-TP has been proposed to induce delayed chain termination at i+3 (i being RDV incorporation position) during RNA synthesis by the core polymerase (Gordon et al., 2020a; Gordon et al., 2020b).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Adding 100 µM RDV-TP in a reaction buffer containing 500 µM NTPs showed a dramatic increase in the pause density and duration, but most of the traces reached the end of the template.
source: Adding 100 µM RDV-TP in a reaction buffer containing 500 µM NTPs showed a dramatic increase in the pause density and duration, but most of the traces reached the end of the template (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The final product length was largely unaffected at all concentrations of RDV-TP.
source: We indeed observed a final product length largely unaffected at all concentrations of RDV-TP (Figure 3B), while the median time for RNA synthesis increased by more than tenfold (Figure 3C), for RDV-TP concentrations increasing up to 300 µM.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The RDV-TP mechanism of action is not termination.
source: Therefore, the RDV-TP mechanism of action is not termination.
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the observation that product length is unaffected by RDV-TP.

claim: The nucleotide addition rate is unaffected by RDV-TP.
source: While the nucleotide addition rate is unaffected by RDV-TP, all pauses are significantly impacted.
evidence: This claim is supported by analysis of dwell time distributions.

claim: The exit rates of Pause 1 and Pause 2 decreased by fourfold and tenfold in the presence of RDV-TP.
source: The exit rates of Pause 1 and Pause 2 decreased by fourfold and tenfold (Figure 3E), while their probabilities increased by twofold and fourfold, respectively (Figure 3F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: RDV-TP incorporation induces polymerase backtrack as deep as ~30 nt.
source: A close observation of the longest-lived pauses clearly demonstrates polymerase backtrack, as deep as ~30 nt (Figure 3GH, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A), demonstrating that RDV incorporation induces polymerase backtrack, which leads to long-lived pauses.
evidence: This claim is supported by direct observation in ultra-stable magnetic tweezers experiments shown in Figure 3G-H.

claim: The almost identical SARS-CoV-1 polymerase demonstrated a similar kinetic signature to RDV-TP incorporation.
source: As expected, the almost identical SARS-CoV-1 polymerase (Kirchdoerfer and Ward, 2019) demonstrated a similar kinetic signature to RDV-TP incorporation (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–F, Supplementary file 1), though to a lesser extent, for example, the backtrack probability increased by ~9-fold when raising RDV-TP concentration up to 300 µM versus 28-fold for SARS-CoV-2 polymerase.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data on SARS-CoV-1 polymerase shown in supplementary figures.

claim: RDV-TP is incorporated by the SNA and VSNA pathways.
source: Therefore, we suggest that RDV-TP is incorporated by the SNA and VSNA pathways (Bera et al., 2021), leading to polymerase backtrack when failing at overcoming the increased energy barrier resulting from the clash of RDV-MP with serine-861.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that RDV-TP affects Pause 1 and Pause 2 exit rates but not their probabilities.

claim: T-1106-TP competes for incorporation against ATP and GTP in a sequence-dependent manner.
source: T-1106-TP competes for incorporation against ATP and GTP in a sequence-dependent manner (Dulin et al., 2017; Shannon et al., 2020b).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Adding 500 µM of T-1106-TP in a reaction buffer containing 500 µM NTPs significantly increased the number and duration of pauses observed in SARS-CoV-2 RNA synthesis activity traces.
source: Adding 500 µM of T-1106-TP in a reaction buffer containing 500 µM NTPs significantly increased the number and duration of pauses observed in SARS-CoV-2 RNA synthesis activity traces (Figure 4A), leading to a 2.6-fold increase in median replication time (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A-B.

claim: The final product length was not affected by T-1106-TP.
source: The final product length was not affected by T-1106-TP, consistent with the T-1106-TP mechanism of action not being terminated (Figure 4C; Dulin et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C and citation to previous work.

claim: Only the Pause 2 exit rate was affected by increasing T-1106-TP concentration, decreasing by tenfold.
source: Investigating how increasing T-1106-TP concentration affects SARS-CoV-2 RNA synthesis kinetics (Figure 4D, Figure 4—figure supplement 1C), we found that only the Pause 2 exit rate was affected, decreasing by tenfold (Figure 4E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: T-1106-TP is incorporated only via the VSNA pathway.
source: Our results suggest an incorporation of T-1106-TP only via the VSNA pathway (Figure 1D), which explains its reduced promiscuity relative to RDV-TP, and is less likely than RDV-TP to induce polymerase backtrack upon incorporation.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that T-1106-TP only affects Pause 2 exit rate.

claim: Sofosbuvir has a proven antiviral effect against hepatitis C virus (HCV) and is an FDA-approved drug to treat HCV infection.
source: Despite its low incorporation rate (Villalba et al., 2020), Sofosbuvir has a proven antiviral effect against hepatitis C virus (HCV) and is an FDA-approved drug to treat HCV infection (Kayali and Schmidt, 2014; Sofia et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Sofosbuvir is incorporated by SARS-CoV-2 polymerase but has no efficacy in infected cells.
source: It is incorporated by SARS-CoV-2 polymerase (Gordon et al., 2020b; Chien et al., 2020), but has no efficacy in infected cells (Xie et al., 2020a).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The presence of 500 µM Sofosbuvir-TP with 500 µM NTP did not affect RNA synthesis by the SARS-CoV-2 polymerase.
source: The presence of 500 µM Sofosbuvir-TP with 500 µM NTP did not affect RNA synthesis by the SARS-CoV-2 polymerase (Figure 5A), while early termination events appeared in the presence of 500 µM 3′-dUTP (Figure 5B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The mean RNA product length of the SARS-CoV-2 polymerase was unaffected by the presence of Sofosbuvir-TP at 500 µM UTP.
source: Supporting this visual observation, the mean RNA product length of the SARS-CoV-2 polymerase was unaffected by the presence of Sofosbuvir-TP (Figure 5C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: SARS-CoV-2 polymerase incorporates on average 3908 nt before incorporating a single Sofosbuvir-TP at 50 µM UTP.
source: In other words, SARS-CoV-2 polymerase incorporates on average 3908 nt and 241 nt before incorporating either a single Sofosbuvir-TP or a single 3′-dUTP, respectively.
evidence: This is a restatement of the effective incorporation rate in more accessible terms.

claim: Stoichiometry against the competing NTP regulates Sofosbuvir-TP and 3′-dUTP incorporation.
source: As for 3′-dATP, our data suggest that stoichiometry against the competing NTP regulates Sofosbuvir-TP and 3′-dUTP incorporation, which therefore support that these analogs utilize the NAB state pathway for incorporation (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that incorporation depends on stoichiometry rather than absolute concentration.

claim: 3ʹ-Deoxy-3′,4ʹ-didehydro-CTP (ddhCTP) is a natural antiviral NA produced in mammalian cells by the viperin-catalyzed conversion of CTP to ddhCTP.
source: 3ʹ-Deoxy-3′,4ʹ-didehydro-CTP (ddhCTP) is a recently discovered natural antiviral NA produced in mammalian cells by the viperin-catalyzed conversion of CTP to ddhCTP using a radical-based mechanism (Gizzi et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work on ddhCTP.

claim: ddhCTP has been shown to efficiently terminate flavivirus replication both in vitro and in cells.
source: While ddhCTP has been shown to efficiently terminate flavivirus replication both in vitro and in cells, its antiviral activity against SARS-CoV-2 polymerase remains unknown.
evidence: This claim is supported by general knowledge about ddhCTP from previous studies.

claim: 3ʹ-dCTP is better incorporated than ddhCTP by SARS-CoV-2 polymerase.
source: These values are similar as what was measured at 500 µM CTP, and confirm the better incorporation of 3ʹ-dCTP over ddhCTP.
evidence: This is inferred from comparison of effective incorporation rates.

claim: Stoichiometry against their competing natural nucleotide CTP directly dictates the incorporation of 3ʹ-dCTP and ddhCTP.
source: Here again, stoichiometry against their competing natural nucleotide CTP directly dictates the incorporation of 3ʹ-dCTP and ddhCTP, further supporting the utilization of the NAB pathway for their incorporation (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that incorporation depends on stoichiometry.

claim: RDV showed a clear antiviral effect with an EC50 of 0.007 µM in Huh7-hACE2 cells infected with SARS-CoV-2.
source: While RDV showed a clear antiviral effect with an EC50 of 0.007 µM (Figure 6—figure supplement 3B), ddhC and Sofosbuvir did not show any impact on SARS-CoV-2 replication in cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by cell-based assay data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3B.

claim: ddhC and Sofosbuvir did not show any impact on SARS-CoV-2 replication in cells.
source: While RDV showed a clear antiviral effect with an EC50 of 0.007 µM (Figure 6—figure supplement 3B), ddhC and Sofosbuvir did not show any impact on SARS-CoV-2 replication in cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by cell-based assay data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claim: A SARS-CoV-2 mutant with amino acid substitutions D90A and E92A that remove the exoribonuclease activity of nsp14 was unable to replicate in cells.
source: This SARS-CoV-2 mutant was unable to replicate in cells (Figure 6—figure supplement 4B–F), confirming a recent report (Ogando et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 4 and citation to previous work.

claim: Pause 1 and Pause 2 exit rates increased by ~3-fold when temperature increased from 25°C to 37°C.
source: Pause 1 and Pause 2 exit rates also increased by ~3-fold (Figure 1H), whereas their respective probabilities increased by twofold and fivefold (Figure 1—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: Pause 1 and Pause 2 probabilities increased by twofold and fivefold respectively when temperature increased from 25°C to 37°C.
source: Pause 1 and Pause 2 exit rates also increased by ~3-fold (Figure 1H), whereas their respective probabilities increased by twofold and fivefold (Figure 1—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2D.

claim: The template contains 250 U (24%), 253 A (24%), 273 C (26%), and 267 G (26%).
source: The template contains 250 U (24%), 253 A (24%), 273 C (26%), and 267 G (26%).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental construct composition.

claim: The RNA hairpin is made of a 499 bp dsRNA stem terminated by a 20 nt loop.
source: The RNA hairpin is made of a 499 bp dsRNA stem terminated by a 20 nt loop that is assembled from three ssRNA annealed together, and two handles, one of 856 bp at the 5′-end and one 822 bp at the 3′-end.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental construct design.

claim: Upon applied force above ~21 pN, the hairpin opens and frees a 1043 nt ssRNA template for SARS-CoV-2 replication.
source: Upon applied force above ~21 pN, the hairpin opens and frees a 1043 nt ssRNA template for SARS-CoV-2 replication.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental method.

claim: The backtrack pause probability increased by ~9-fold for SARS-CoV-1 polymerase when raising RDV-TP concentration up to 300 µM.
source: As expected, the almost identical SARS-CoV-1 polymerase (Kirchdoerfer and Ward, 2019) demonstrated a similar kinetic signature to RDV-TP incorporation (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–F, Supplementary file 1), though to a lesser extent, for example, the backtrack probability increased by ~9-fold when raising RDV-TP concentration up to 300 µM versus 28-fold for SARS-CoV-2 polymerase.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data on SARS-CoV-1 shown in supplementary figures.

claim: Lowering ATP concentration increases the potency of RDV-TP by dramatically increasing the backtrack pause probability.
source: Interestingly, lowering ATP concentration increases the potency of RDV-TP by dramatically increasing the backtrack pause probability.
evidence: This is inferred from experimental observations at different ATP concentrations.

claim: The backtrack pause probability increased by 43-fold at low ATP and RDV-TP concentrations versus 18-fold at high ATP and RDV-TP concentrations.
source: Most remarkably, the backtrack pause probability increased dramatically at low ATP and RDV-TP concentrations, even more so than at high ATP and RDV-TP concentrations, that is, 43-fold versus 18-fold, respectively (Figure 3—figure supplement 3F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3F.

claim: The increased energy barrier induced by the steric clash of RDV-TP with the nsp12 serine-861 reduces dramatically the likelihood of a successful forward translocation of the polymerase.
source: However, we know such a pause is catalytically incompetent (Bera et al., 2021), and therefore the increase of the backtrack probability is an illustration of the effect of RDV-TP incorporation at low nucleotide concentration: the increased energy barrier induced by the steric clash of RDV-TP with the nsp12 serine-861 reduces dramatically the likelihood of a successful forward translocation of the polymerase (Gordon et al., 2020b; Kokic et al., 2021).
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental observations and cited structural studies.

claim: Pause 1 and Pause 2 probabilities were unaffected by the presence of RDV-TP at 37°C.
source: On the other hand, Pause 1 and Pause 2 probabilities were unaffected by the presence of RDV-TP (Figure 3—figure supplement 4C), supporting the notion that the increase in probability in the experiments performed at 25°C was the consequence of the polymerase backtrack pause distribution biasing Pause 1 and Pause 2 distributions (Dulin et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4C.

claim: The same NA may have a different mechanism of action on different RdRps.
source: These observations contrast with our previous findings with poliovirus RdRp (Dulin et al., 2017), where T-1106 incorporation induced deep polymerase backtrack. Therefore, the same NA may have a different mechanism of action on different RdRps.
evidence: This is inferred from comparison of results with different viral polymerases.

claim: Under certain conditions, the interferon α-induced viperin converts up to 30% of the cellular pool of CTP into ddhCTP.
source: Furthermore, under certain conditions, the interferon α-induced viperin converts up to 30% of the cellular pool of CTP into ddhCTP, further increasing the ddhCTP:CTP stoichiometry in a direction favoring even greater potency (Gizzi et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work on viperin.

claim: Pyrimidine-based analogs will only need to compete with intracellular CTP pools on the order of 100 µM.
source: In contrast, pyrimidine-based analogs, for example, derivatives of CTP, will only need to compete with intracellular CTP pools on the order of 100 µM (Traut, 1994).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work on cellular nucleotide pools.

claim: NAs modified at the 2′ and 3′ positions are strongly discriminated against by their competing natural nucleotide.
source: A steady-state kinetic study showed that NAs modified at the 2′ and 3′ positions are strongly discriminated against by their competing natural nucleotide (Gordon et al., 2020b).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous kinetic studies.

claim: Polymerase backtrack is not an intermediate of product strand proofreading.
source: Our results suggest that polymerase backtrack is therefore not an intermediate of product strand proofreading, which corroborates a preceding study showing that nsp14 poorly excise single-stranded RNA (Ferron et al., 2018; Liu et al., 2021).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that RDV is effective despite nsp14 presence, and supported by citations.

claim: The location of the modification in the ribose or in the base dictates the catalytic pathway(s) used for NA incorporation.
source: We reveal that the location of the modification in the ribose or in the base dictates the catalytic pathway(s) used for its incorporation.
evidence: This is a general conclusion inferred from comparing different NAs with modifications at different positions.

claim: RDV incorporation leads to long-lived pauses that may appear as termination in traditional ensemble assays.
source: We show that RDV incorporation does not terminate viral RNA synthesis, but leads the polymerase into backtrack as far as 30 nt, which may appear as termination in traditional ensemble assays.
evidence: This is inferred from single-molecule observations compared to expected ensemble assay results.

claim: The polymerase incorporates ddhCTP well in vitro.
source: SARS-CoV-2 is able to evade the endogenously synthesized product of the viperin antiviral protein, ddhCTP, though the polymerase incorporates this NA well.
evidence: This claim is supported by the measured effective incorporation rates for ddhCTP.

claim: Tension does not play a significant role in RDV-TP incorporation.
source: We did not observe any significant difference between the two experiments at 35 pN and 25 pN (Figure 2—figure supplement 4C,D), indicating that tension does not play a significant role in RDV-TP incorporation.
evidence: This is inferred from comparison of experiments at different applied forces.

claim: The applied tension has no influence in the incorporation of Sofosbuvir-TP.
source: Repeating the experiments for a Sofosbuvir-TP:UTP stoichiometry of 6 now at 25 pN tension (Figure 2—figure supplement 4A), we did not see a significant difference in comparison with the data at 35 pN (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E–H), therefore the applied tension has no influence in the incorporation of Sofosbuvir-TP.
evidence: This is inferred from comparison of experiments at different applied forces.

claim: The applied tension does not affect ddhCTP incorporation.
source: We also did not observe any impact of the applied tension for ddhCTP incorporation (Figure 2—figure supplement 4A).
evidence: This is inferred from comparison of experiments at different applied forces.

claim: NA selection and incorporation are not force-dependent.
source: The present study demonstrates that NA selection and incorporation are not force-dependent (Figure 2—figure supplement 4), which further validates the utilization of high-throughput magnetic tweezers to study NA mechanism of action.
evidence: This is a general conclusion inferred from experiments at different forces.

claim: RDV efficacy is further amplified when the polymerase is elongating through template secondary structures.
source: We anticipate that RDV efficacy is further amplified when the polymerase is elongating through template secondary structures, which stimulates polymerase backtrack (Bera et al., 2021).
evidence: This is speculation based on known effects of secondary structures and RDV mechanism.

claim: nsp14 poorly excises single-stranded RNA.
source: Our results suggest that polymerase backtrack is therefore not an intermediate of product strand proofreading, which corroborates a preceding study showing that nsp14 poorly excise single-stranded RNA (Ferron et al., 2018; Liu et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: 3′-dNTP is cytotoxic.
source: Though well incorporated, 3′-dNTP is cytotoxic, and is therefore not used as antiviral drugs (Arnold et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: RDV-TP is better incorporated than Favipiravir by SARS-CoV-2 polymerase.
source: Finally, Pause 1 and Pause 2 respectively account for ~6% and ~0.3% of all the nucleotide addition events at a saturating concentration of NTP. This defines an upper limit for RDV-TP and T-1106-TP relative incorporation, and explains why RDV-TP is incorporated much better than Favipiravir (Xie et al., 2020a).
evidence: This is inferred from the pathway analysis and supported by citation.

claim: RDV-TP is incorporated threefold better than ATP at submicromolar concentration of NTPs.
source: In the first one, the experiments were performed at submicromolar concentration of NTPs, and showed that RDV-TP is incorporated threefold better than ATP in such conditions (Gordon et al., 2020b).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous ensemble kinetic studies.

claim: RDV is better incorporated by the coronavirus polymerase elongation kinetics at low concentration of natural nucleotides.
source: Both of these studies agree with our results: RDV is better incorporated by the coronavirus polymerase elongation kinetics at low concentration of natural nucleotides.
evidence: This is a synthesis of results from this study and previous cited studies.

claim: The barrier induced by the clash of RDV-MP with serine-861 is sufficiently strong to elicit polymerase backtrack.
source: Our assay revealed that RDV-TP incorporation leads the coronavirus polymerase into backtrack as deep as ~30 nt (Figure 3GH). This result demonstrates that the barrier induced by the clash of RDV-MP (Kokic et al., 2021) with the serine-861 of nsp12 is sufficiently strong to elicit polymerase backtrack, leading the polymerase into a pause long enough to be mistaken for a termination event in ensemble assays.
evidence: This is inferred from experimental observations and supported by citation to structural studies.

claim: RDV has a strong efficacy against SARS-CoV-2 in infected cells.
source: Interestingly, RDV has a strong efficacy against SARS-CoV-2 in infected cells (Figure 6—figure supplement 4A,B), which indicates that the 3′–5′ exonuclease nsp14 does not remove efficiently RDV-MP from the nucleic acid chain.
evidence: This claim is supported by cell-based assay data shown in supplementary figures.

claim: The 3′–5′ exonuclease nsp14 does not remove efficiently RDV-MP from the nucleic acid chain.
source: Interestingly, RDV has a strong efficacy against SARS-CoV-2 in infected cells (Figure 6—figure supplement 4A,B), which indicates that the 3′–5′ exonuclease nsp14 does not remove efficiently RDV-MP from the nucleic acid chain.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that RDV is effective in cells despite nsp14 presence.
